sanskrit: ati viśvāḥ pariṣṭhā stena iva vrajam akramīt | oṣadhayaḥ pracucyavur yat kiṃ ca tanvo rapaḥ ||
english: Like a thief that has broken through all enclosures into the fold, the herbs have shaken loose whatsoever blemish there is upon the body.

sanskrit: yasyauṣadhayaḥ prasarpatha- -aṅgam aṅgaṃ paruṣ paruḥ | tasmād yakṣmaṃ vi bādhadhvam ugro madhyamaśīr iva ||
english: O herbs, as ye creep through limb by limb, joint by joint, drive out from him the yakṣma, as the fierce one who strikes from the middle.

sanskrit: anyā vo anyām avatv anyānyasyā upāvata | oṣadhayaḥ saṃvidānā idaṃ me prāvatā vacaḥ ||
english: Let one of you aid another; let each come to the assistance of the other. O herbs, being of one accord, favor this my word.

sanskrit: avapatantīr apadaṃ diva oṣadhayas pari | yaṃ jīvam aśnavāmahai na sa riṣyāti pūruṣaḥ ||
english: The herbs, descending footlessly from heaven all around — whichever living man we lay hold of with them, that man shall not be harmed.

sanskrit: yā oṣadhayaḥ somarājñīr bahvīḥ śatavicakṣaṇāḥ | bṛhaspatiprasūtās tā no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: The herbs that are queens of Soma, the many possessed of a hundredfold discernment, sent forth by Bṛhaspati — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: yāḥ phalinīr yā aphalā akośā yāś ca keśinīḥ | bṛhaspatiprasūtās tā no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Those that bear fruit, those that are fruitless, those that lack a sheath, and those that are leafy — sent forth by Bṛhaspati, may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: jīvalāṃ naghāriṣām ā te badhnāmy oṣadhim | yā ta āyur upāharād apa rakṣāṃsi cātayāt ||
english: I bind upon thee the herb Jīvalā, the Naghāriṣā — that which shall bring thee life and drive the rakṣas away.

sanskrit: kālo aśvo vahati saptaraśmiḥ sahasrākṣo ajaro bhūriretāḥ | tām ā rohanti kavayo vipaścitas tasya cakrā bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: Kāla, the horse with seven reins, carries on — thousand-eyed, unaging, of abundant seed. The seers, the far-seeing, mount him; his wheels are all the worlds.

sanskrit: sapta cakrān vahati kāla eṣa saptāsya nābhīr amṛtaṃ nv akṣaḥ | sa imā viśvā bhuvanāny añjan kālaḥ sa īyate prathamo nu devaḥ ||
english: This Kāla draws seven wheels; seven are his nave-hubs; his axle is immortality. He, encompassing all these worlds, Kāla, moves on — he is verily the foremost god.

sanskrit: pūrṇaḥ kumbho adhi kāla āhitas taṃ vai paśyāmo bahudhā nu santam | sa imā viśvā bhuvanāni pratyaṅ kālaṃ tam āhuḥ parame vyoman ||
english: A full jar has been placed upon Kāla; him we behold as existing in many forms. He, facing all these worlds — they call that Kāla in the highest heaven.

sanskrit: sa eva san bhuvanāny ābharat sa eva san bhuvanāni pary ait | pitā sann abhavat putra eṣāṃ tasmād vai nānyat param asti tejaḥ ||
english: He alone, being present, upheld the worlds; he alone, being present, encompassed the worlds. Being their father, he became their son — therefore there is no higher radiance than he.

sanskrit: kālo 'mūṃ divam ajanayat kala imāṃ pṛthivīm uta | kālena bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ ca- -iṣitaṃ ha vi tiṣṭhate ||
english: Kāla generated yonder heaven; Kāla also generated this earth. By Kāla, the past and the future, impelled, stand spread forth.

sanskrit: kālo bhūtim asṛjat kale tapati sūryaḥ | kālo ha viśvā bhūtāni kāle cakṣur vi paśyati ||
english: Kāla created prosperity; in Kāla the sun blazes. In Kāla are all beings; in Kāla the eye sees far.

sanskrit: kāle manaḥ kāle prāṇaḥ kāle nāma samāhitam | kālena sarvā nandanty āgatena prajā imāḥ ||
english: In Kāla is mind; in Kāla is breath; in Kāla is name gathered up. By Kāla arrived, all these creatures rejoice.

sanskrit: kāle tapaḥ kāle jyeṣṭhaṃ kāle brahma samāhitam | kālo ha sarvasyeśvaro yaḥ pitāsīt prajāpateḥ ||
english: In Kāla is austerity; in Kāla is the exalted; in Kāla brahman is gathered. Kāla is verily the lord of all — he who was the father of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: teneṣitaṃ tena jātaṃ tad u tasmin pratiṣṭhitam | kālo ha brahma bhūtvā bibharti parameṣṭhinam ||
english: By him it is impelled; by him it is born; in him, moreover, it is established. Kāla, having become brahman, sustains Parameṣṭhin.

sanskrit: kālaḥ prajām asṛjata kālo agre prajāpatim | svayambhūḥ kaśyapaḥ kālāt tapaḥ kālād ajāyata ||
english: Kāla generated creatures; Kāla in the beginning generated Prajāpati. The self-existent Kaśyapa and austerity — from Kāla they were born.

sanskrit: kālād āpaḥ sam abhavan kālād brahma tapo diśaḥ | kālenod eti sūryaḥ kāle ni viśate punaḥ ||
english: From Kāla the waters came together; from Kāla brahman, austerity, and the directions. By Kāla the sun rises; in Kāla he enters again.

sanskrit: kālena vātaḥ pavate kālena pṛthivī mahī dyaur mahī kāla āhitā | kālo ha bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ ca putro ajanayat puraḥ ||
english: By Kāla the wind blows; by Kāla the great earth and the great heaven are established in Kāla. Kāla indeed begat the past and the future as his sons before all.

sanskrit: kālād ṛcaḥ sam abhavan yajuṣ kālād ajāyata | kālo yajñaṃ sam airayad devebhyo bhāgam akṣitam ||
english: From Kāla the ṛc-verses came together; the yajus was born from Kāla. Kāla set in motion the sacrifice, the imperishable share belonging to the gods.

sanskrit: kāle gandharvāpsarasaḥ kāle lokāḥ samāhitāḥ | kāle 'yam aṅgirā devo atharvā cādhi tiṣṭhataḥ ||
english: In Kāla are the Gandharvāpsarases; in Kāla the worlds are gathered. In Kāla this divine Aṅgiras and Atharvan stand supreme.

sanskrit: imaṃ ca lokaṃ paramaṃ ca lokaṃ puṇyāṃś ca lokān vidhṛtīś ca puṇyāḥ | sarvām̐l lokān abhijitya brahmaṇā kālaḥ sa īyate paramo nu devaḥ ||
english: This world and the highest world, the blessed worlds and the blessed sustaining powers — having conquered all worlds with brahman, that Kāla moves on: he is verily the supreme god.
